tags: why does my dog sleep on my clothes
script: You take off a sweater, drop it on the floor for two minutes, and come back to find your dog curled up on top of it like it's the most comfortable bed in the house. This comes down almost entirely to scent. A dog's sense of smell is dramatically more powerful than ours, and your scent specifically is one of the most comforting things in their entire world. Clothing that's been worn holds a concentrated version of that scent, far stronger than anything else lying around the house, including their actual dog bed. Sleeping surrounded by your smell can genuinely lower a dog's stress levels, it's part of why this habit tends to get even more noticeable when you've been away from home, traveling, or working longer hours than usual. It's also just warm and soft, which never hurts. For dogs with any separation anxiety, this behavior often becomes more frequent specifically on days when you've been gone longer, since your scent is doing double duty as both comfort and a kind of placeholder for your presence. So next time your laundry disappears under a sleeping dog, know that it's really just a very sincere compliment.
